newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedbank says plans to buy 7.4 pct Hoiupank stake.
newsitem.headline: Swedbank says plans to buy 7.4 pct Hoiupank stake.

text.p: Swedish commercial bank Swedbank said on Wednesday it was in the process of acquiring 7.4 percent of the shares in Estonian bank Hoiupank from the central bank of Estonia.
"This will make Swedbank the single largest owner in Hoiupank with a total of 19.9 percent of the shares," Swedbank said in a statement.
After the deal the second largest owner would be the European development bank EBRD, which has a 17 percent stake in Hoiupank.
The Estonian central bank, the Bank of Estonia, would for the time being retain its 6.2 percent stake, Swedbank said.
The sale of shares to Swedbank is part of the Bank of Estonia's gradual divestment of Hoiupank, it said.

"The deal is an indication of our increased faith in Hoiupank and in the Estonian market which is of growing interest also to our corporate customers," Swedbank vice president Hakan Kallaker said in the statement.

"Our increased engagement in Hoiupank is also in line with our strategy for the Nordic countries and the Baltic region with enhanced cooperation, partnerships and local presence on the various markets," he added.
